name: 13-day-threshold-unreachable
incident: cam-E 192.168.1.100 + cam-F 192.168.1.100, 2026-08-16 afternoon (and cam-D the same morning)
description:
A dim room whose day pipeline never gets under total_gain_day_threshold. The machine's behaviour here is CORRECT and this scenario asserts that it stays correct - what it pins is the diagnostic, because the behaviour is indistinguishable from a stuck camera unless the log says why.

Three cameras hit this in one day. cam-E: default threshold 300, day-pipeline gain 700 -> 591 -> 531 across a fifteen-minute excursion, best 531 = 1.77x the threshold, so the probe reverted and the camera sat in night mode all afternoon. cam-F: threshold 450, day pipeline 3299 -> 2629 -> 2250, best 2250 = 5.0x. cam-D that morning: same shape, fixed by hand with total_gain_day_threshold = 700. In every case the machine did exactly what it was told - the day pipeline is the trustworthy judge, it judged 'not day', and night is the recoverable side - and in every case the diagnosis cost an SSH session and a manual read of day-pipeline gains out of syslog, because the revert logs 'unverified day, gain N' and never names the threshold that made it unverifiable.

This is generator C applied to a CONFIG bar rather than a derived one. dn_bar_check() has never looked at total_gain_day_threshold because it is not derived from a measurement - but it fails identically: set below what a scene's day pipeline can produce, the comparison it gates can never come true, and the path is silently dead. The difference is that a derived bar can be re-derived, while this one sits there until a human edits it, so the machine will spend one audible IR-cut pair per reconfirm interval, all day, forever.

The warn is opt-in (daynight.diagnose_thresholds, default 0) - it reports a real misconfiguration but fires once per reconfirm interval forever until a human edits the config, which is pure log growth on a fleet that does not need it. Scenario 14 is the default-off twin. Beyond the opt-in the warn is gated on DN_DAY_THR_UNREACHABLE (1.5x) rather than a bare >, so a dawn ramp stays quiet: a ramp's best reading sits just above the threshold and crosses it a probe or two later, while a mis-set threshold is missed by a wide factor. Corpus 09 is the negative control for that and must not emit this line. RESTATED 2026-08-17: a single failed probe cannot distinguish 'this room is dark' from 'day_gain is unreachable', which is why the warning now waits for three consecutive failed probes and says which of the two it might be, instead of asserting the second. It is also latched once per session rather than repeating per probe.

expect_log: no probe has ever confirmed day \(\d+ in a row found night\)
